text: {"observations":"Tonal, harmonic calls with gliding pitch: an arched rise-fall contour at about 0.5-1.8 s (fundamental roughly 400-500 Hz with harmonics up to ~3.2 kHz), then a long drawn-out call at about 3.2-6.5 s whose fundamental falls from ~450 Hz to ~200 Hz, and a lower wavering call at about 7-9.5 s. Broadband noisy bursts around 2.5-3 s could be a hiss. The fundamental is too high and the contour too melodic for a cow's moo (rules out D); there are no short broadband barks (argues against B); pitch is too low and the calls too long for typical birdsong (argues against C). The rise-fall meow shape and drawn-out falling yowl fit a cat best, though a dog howl cannot be fully excluded.","answer":"A"}
